bullets.title: 10yr at 5.35%, S&P near range top — rates vs. equities divergence widening
bullets.body: The 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.35% (+7bps on the day), a new cycle high, with Hedgeye targeting 5.13–5.38% range and seeing the next leg higher. S&P futures +0.41% to 7,842 — near Hedgeye's range top of 7,851 — while the bond market is pricing financial stress (CMBS special servicing at 11.42%, BDC distressed debt up 25% YoY) that equities are ignoring. Investor consensus per 22V pegs 10yr at 5.1% by year-end and S&P above 8,000, but the growing asset-class divergence is a key risk flag.

bullets.title: Q3 earnings setup: record positive pre-announcements, 29.5% EPS growth expected
bullets.body: JPMorgan notes Q3 2026 has the largest number of positive pre-announcements on record, led by Tech, Industrials, and Healthcare; all 11 S&P sectors expected to show positive revenue and earnings growth with 12.3% revenue growth and 29.5% EPS growth. Margins at 15% are the second-best ever. Goldman's sector specialists flag that the mark-to-market gains from mega-cap tech that boosted EPS 12% last quarter will largely disappear in Q3, a meaningful headwind to aggregate beats.

bullets.title: AI capex sustainability hinges on $400-600B ARR by end-2027; Anthropic IPO is the key catalyst
bullets.body: 22V frames the critical question: frontier-lab and AI product ARR must reach $400–600B by end-2027 to underwrite capex plans through 2028–29, with visibility to ~$1T annualized ARR in 2028–29 needed for financing sustainability. Anthropic's IPO revenue commentary is described as the single most important near-term catalyst for the AI buildout investment thesis. AI capex contributed roughly 50bps to aggregate demand growth inclusive of trade drag, but hardware is almost entirely importable, making net domestic demand contribution slightly negative.

bullets.title: Texas regulatory risk is a grey rhino for AI data center buildout — Abbott race tightening
bullets.body: Texas hosts ~35–40% of US AI factory buildout capacity through 2030, and the Abbott gubernatorial race is described as 'trending directionally the wrong way' heading into early voting on Oct 19. Additionally, grassroots opposition is rising: PA data center moratorium protests and chaotic Memphis hearings signal ground-up regulatory risk that consensus is underweighting. Base case remains Abbott wins and environment normalizes post-election, but this is flagged as a key tail risk for data center capex names.

bullets.title: SpaceX GPU build (200k GPUs in 9 months) pressures neocloud/DC stocks near-term
bullets.body: SpaceX built 200k GPU capacity (300–500MW) in 9 months vs. the market's typical 18–36 months for 100MW, creating faster and cheaper compute supply that competes directly with traditional data center operators. Google's AI infra chief says power lead times are the key constraint; Google is targeting a 6-month doubling of token-serving capacity with aging TPUs at 100% utilization and signed a new deal with CEG for power. This dynamic is cited as the catalyst for neocloud/DC knee-jerk selling in pre-market.

bullets.title: MRVL Analyst Day: raises FY28 target to $20B, projects $70-90B by FY31 at 55-60% CAGR
bullets.body: Marvell raised its FY28 revenue target to $20B (vs. prior ~$18B and consensus $18.2B) and set a long-term FY31 model of $70–90B revenue, >$30 EPS, and >36% FCF margin on custom XPU and optical interconnect strength. FY29 custom revenue target is $12B+, with a FY31 midpoint of $30B (75–85% CAGR). Sell-side consensus is 90% Buy; average PT raised +13% to $337; Piper raised to $400. Shares were +5.8% post-event.

bullets.title: Micron Taiwan union votes to strike — semiconductor supply risk flagged
bullets.body: Micron's Taiwan labor union voted in favor of a strike after workers rejected the FY26 bonus package amid profit-sharing disputes. MU shares were -2.6% in pre-market. Separately, DA Davidson raised its MU price target to $3,000 (from $2,100), arguing AI inference is increasingly memory-constrained and demand will exceed supply through 2027–28, with strategic contracts covering ~50% of volume providing visibility.

bullets.title: Rates hitting mortgage market hard: 30yr at 7.49%, purchase apps -2.1% w/w
bullets.body: 30-year mortgage rates rose to 7.49% (highest since November 2023), pushing mortgage applications down 4.2% w/w with purchase apps -2.1%. MBA purchase applications are trending lower with housing turnover severely pressured by rate lock effects. EFX and FICO derive ~20% of revenue from mortgage, TRU ~12% — all facing a direct headwind.

bullets.title: Hedgeye Quad 2 posture: long XLK/quantum/software, short Russell 2000, TLT, and utilities
bullets.body: Hedgeye maintains a Quad 2 (rising growth, rising inflation) framework with the 10yr at a cycle high of 5.33% and expects new highs. Key trades: long XLK, quantum computing, and software; short Russell 2000 (IWM), long-term bonds (TLT/ZROZ/LQD), and utilities (XLU puts on 3% rally). S&P 500 risk range is 7,676–7,851; they discourage being long near the upper boundary. Separately, Hedgeye's ETF re-rank shows ETHA (+16), IBIT (+11), and QTUM (+6) as top movers with McCullough adding 100bps ETHA and 50bps each IBIT and QTUM.

bullets.title: Broad market breadth deteriorating: 29% of Russell 3000 down 30%+, momentum factor vulnerable
bullets.body: Despite Nasdaq earnings growth of ~36% supporting near-record highs, 29% of Russell 3000 stocks are in drawdowns of 30% or more. JPMorgan notes the momentum factor is vulnerable near-term (Democratic factor up ~20% since August). Tech is experiencing its fastest single-stock selling pace since 2008, with flows turning negative for the first time since July. KOSPI is down 25.3% from its June peak, cited as an early signal that AI bubble dynamics are already deflating in some markets.

bullets.title: Consumer spending resilient: Redbook +8.6% YoY, mall traffic +5.6%, card data mixed
bullets.body: Redbook retail sales accelerated to +8.6% YoY (~100–200bps above FY25 levels) and September mall traffic was up 5.6% YoY (open-air) and 5.5% (indoor). However, credit card spending fell 6% in September (third consecutive annual decline), and consumer stocks in Walmart, TJX, and American Express are weakening — signaling divergent stress signals across income cohorts.

bullets.title: Non-core inflation transmission: energy hits producer costs in 2-3 quarters; US tariff disinflation a partial offset
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's framework shows energy shocks move beyond headline CPI into producer costs within 2–3 quarters, with diesel as the broadest second-round channel. Food inflation is slower but more persistent; shipping, chips, and metals are adding to producer costs but the current environment is less severe than 2021 (softer demand, tighter policy, less synchronized disruptions). In the US specifically, tariff disinflation is expected to offset part of the energy-led producer-price impulse.

bullets.title: GS 3Q earnings preview: hyperscaler ROIC, AI follow-through, and capital markets cycle are key debates
bullets.body: Goldman's sector specialists flag three cross-sector themes for 3Q earnings: (1) hyperscalers face scrutiny on maintaining Q2 ROIC momentum given 2027 capex expectations; (2) semi/AI stocks need earnings follow-through after limited 2Q performance, with 'Personal AI Assistants' as the bull case bridging to 2028 visibility; (3) capital markets activity slowdown raises the late-cycle vs. temporary air-pocket question amid rising rates. Internet sentiment may be oversold into 3Q with few bottom-fishing calls on travel/commerce.

bullets.title: AI financing boom crowding out traditional HY borrowers; distressed leveraged loans at pandemic highs
bullets.body: AI-related financing is crowding out traditional high-yield borrowers, with non-AI issuance down 21% YoY. JPMorgan flags distressed leveraged loans at $65B — highest since March 2020 — with tech accounting for 39% of distressed loans. BDC distressed debt is rising (583 BDC-held companies showing credit pressure, up 25% from year-end 2025), and CMBS loans in special servicing hit 11.42%, highest since 2013.

bullets.title: Wireless Q3 setup positive but Starlink, AI Muse, and rate fears overhang investor sentiment
bullets.body: TD Cowen and KeyBanc both flag positive Q3 wireless fundamentals — tame competition, muted churn, limited iPhone impact — but investor anxiety is elevated around Starlink Mobile launch, Meta's AI Muse price-search tool (AI-driven plan comparison threatening ARPU), and rising interest rates pressuring rate-sensitive carriers. TD Cowen maintains Buy on TMUS and VZ, Hold on T; KeyBanc is Overweight T and TMUS, Sector Weight VZ.

bullets.title: Cable faces structural headwinds from fiber/FWA; CMCSA subscriber losses worse than expected
bullets.body: KeyBanc's Q3 broadband survey shows fiber and FWA (telco) offering faster speeds at similar or lower prices than cable, with telco taking ongoing market share. TD Cowen also flags AI Muse as an ARPU risk and expects FTTH/FWA trends to continue for an extended period. CMCSA reported worse-than-expected subscriber losses in September. Both firms maintain Buys on CHTR and CMCSA citing valuation, but KeyBanc is underweight CMCSA.

bullets.title: IPPs surge on data center PPA execution; BKH wins 2.7GW Google Wyoming deal
bullets.body: CEG, VST, and TLN showed a sentiment pivot on their ability to execute data center PPAs without 1-for-1 PJM capacity requirements. Black Hills Corp (BKH) won a Google Wyoming data center deal with a 2.7GW resource mix, expecting $150M net income in 2030 and $2.4B unlevered FCF. Despite recent strength, IPPs appear to be trading with no incremental contracting upside priced in.

bullets.title: Brokers & crypto: first EPS estimate upgrades since 4Q25; valuations near trough
bullets.body: Goldman increased 2027E/28E adjusted EPS by a median 5%/6% across the brokers and crypto group — the first positive earnings revisions since Q4 2025. Digital asset-skewed firms trade at below the 5th percentile of historical multiples; the group rose 11% on average in Q3, outperforming S&P 500 by ~5pp. Consensus crypto estimates are positively inflecting with key themes around retail trading recovery and blockchain/agentic commerce monetization.

bullets.title: Kantro shifts Macro Select Model to long for first time in over a year; favors Quality as cycle peaks
bullets.body: Kantro changed his Macro Select Model to long for the first time in over a year, citing earnings growth and breadth at 5-year highs. However, forward-looking indicators suggest economic momentum (PMIs) is near a peak, and quality factors are expected to outperform as the cycle matures past peak growth — a shift in factor positioning from momentum.

bullets.title: Brent above $100/bbl on Iran-Hormuz escalation; tightening global oil supplies
bullets.body: Global oil supplies are tightening with Brent above $100/bbl amid Iran escalation in the Hormuz strait, cited by JPMorgan as a macro risk alongside elevated WTI at $90.09 in pre-market. Hedgeye is long Brent crude and BWET (tanker shipping) as inflationary exposures. Refining 3Q earnings are at record levels but face near-term headwinds from diesel price highs, valuation concerns, and potential policy controls on exports.
